title: Company record
description: One cybersecurity or information security provider in the Norway directory. One file per company, named after its id. Fields holding numbers must always carry a source; unknown facts are omitted or null rather than guessed. `scripts/validate.py` is the authoritative enforcement of these rules.

id.description: Slug, must match the file name (data/companies/<id>.json).

name.description: Name as buyers know it. Keep the name used in the original pentest list so the lineage stays traceable; use `notes` for renames.

legal_name.description: Registered legal name of the Norwegian entity, from Enhetsregisteret.

website.description: Official site. Must have been loaded and confirmed to belong to the company.

category.description: norwegian = headquartered or registered in Norway; nordic = Nordic group with a Norwegian presence; international = sells to Norway without a Norwegian entity.

org_nr.description: Norwegian organisasjonsnummer for the entity that delivers the Norwegian work. Unique across the dataset, confirmed by a human against Enhetsregisteret, because the registry's name search is fuzzy.

office_in_norway.description: True only with a registered Norwegian entity or a Norwegian address published by the company. False means no Norwegian entity was found, never 'no Norwegian staff'.

office_cities.description: Norwegian cities the company is registered in or publishes as offices.

employees_total.description: Headcount the company itself states on its own about or careers page. Requires employees_source. This is a whole-company figure, not a count of security staff.

employees_note.description: Qualifier on the figure, e.g. 'stated as 170+' or 'group-wide across the Nordics'.

brreg_employees.description: Headcount reported to Enhetsregisteret for this legal entity. It covers the whole entity, including staff who have nothing to do with security, so it is never used as a security staff count. Refreshed by scripts/enrich_brreg.py.

brreg_employees_as_of.description: Registry registration date for the headcount, so staleness is visible.

security_staff.description: In-house cybersecurity staff: consultants, testers, analysts and engineers on the payroll of the company itself. The most decision-relevant figure in the dataset and the primary ordering signal. Requires security_staff_source and security_staff_basis. Left null when unknown, which is the common case, rather than guessed. Never taken from the registry, and a crowdsourced platform's researcher pool is not staff.

security_staff_basis.description: What kind of claim the number is: company-site = the company publishes it, which is confirmed; attestation = a named person who works there or with them vouches for it first-hand, which is also confirmed but weaker on paper; estimate = the list maintainer's own guarded estimate from market knowledge with nobody standing behind it, so it is labelled estimated everywhere; crowd-platform = a crowdsourced platform's contracted researcher pool, which is not staff. Required whenever security_staff is set.

security_staff_is_minimum.description: True when the figure is a floor rather than an exact count, e.g. '17+'. Rendered as 17+.

security_staff_scope.description: What the figure counts when it is not a clean security-only number: security-and-it = the team also does general IT, whole-company = the company states a company-wide figure that includes security staff. Keeps a broad number from reading as a narrow one.

security_staff_note.description: What the company does publish instead, e.g. 'publishes 170+ employees and a Red Team service but no staff count'.

delivery.description: How the Norwegian work is actually delivered: in-house = the company's own employees do it; mixed = mostly own staff with subcontractors for peaks or specialisms; partner-network = there is no real delivery team, work is resold or subcontracted to another provider; unknown = not established. This is the field that separates a provider from a reseller. Requires delivery_source when set.

delivery_note.description: How the delivery model was established, and anything a reader needs to interpret it.

specialty.description: One factual line on what this company is actually known for, in plain language, no marketing. Shown as the first line of the capabilities column.

capabilities.description: The capability tags: what the company itself says it can do. Only add what the company offers, from its own pages. This is the column buyers filter on.

certifications.description: Certifications and approvals the company publishes, e.g. ISO 27001, CREST, NSM-approved incident response.

former_names.description: Rename history from Enhetsregisteret. Omit when the pinned org_nr belongs to an acquiring company rather than the listed one.

notes.description: Renames, acquisitions, corrections against the original list, and anything a reader needs to interpret the row.

verification.description: verified = the facts stated were checked against a primary source; partial = some fields still need confirming (see notes); unverified = no verifiable presence was found.

last_verified.description: Date a human last checked this row. CI warns after 12 months and fails after 24.

verified_by.description: Who checked it, e.g. a GitHub handle.

sources.description: Evidence. At least one entry per company; every number needs its own.

type.description: registry = Enhetsregisteret; company-site = the company's own page; news = third-party reporting; seed-list = the original blog list this directory grew out of; attestation = a named person vouches for the claim first-hand, and the note must say who and why they would know; estimate = the maintainer's own guarded estimate from market knowledge rather than a source, and the note must say so.
